intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning coastlines along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail, stopping at Praia da Marinha's golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear turquoise waters for swimming and snorkeling among sea caves and rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit boutique wineries in the Lagoa wine region, tasting local Algarve DOC wines including Arinto, Negra Mole, and Syrah varieties. Guided tours include cellar visits, food pairings with local cheeses and charcuterie, and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through dramatic sea caves and grottos along the Algarve coastline, culminating at the famous Benagil Cave with its natural skylight dome. A guided kayak tour offers access to hidden beaches and sea arches unreachable on foot.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffside Experience
experiences.description: Visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, and the historic Sagres Fortress at golden hour. Watch the sun dip into the Atlantic from towering 75-meter cliffs while exploring the 15th-century fortress used by Henry the Navigator.

experiences.name: Quinta do Francês Organic Wine Tasting
experiences.description: Experience an intimate organic winery tasting session at one of the Algarve's most acclaimed small-production estates. Sample award-winning red and white wines paired with local Algarve honey, figs, and artisan bread while learning about sustainable viticulture practices.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Take the affordable Aerobus or local bus to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with your beachfront surroundings. Grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or hotel vending area.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: N/A - in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from convenience store near hotel or airport grab-and-go options before departure — budget under €5

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport to Algarve coastal areas: take the EVA Bus or Aerobus for around €2-4. Pre-book a taxi only if buses are not running at that hour (approx €15-20). Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, head straight to the beachfront just outside Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxed morning swim and explore the immediate shoreline. September water temperatures in the Algarve are warm and perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a local bus to the nearest town center (likely Lagos, Albufeira, or Portimão depending on exact resort location). Explore the old town on foot — visit the local market, admire the azulejo-tiled churches, and wander cobblestone streets. Pick up a regional map from the tourist office (free).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the marina or seafront promenade. Watch the sunset from a clifftop viewpoint. Head back to a local tasca (traditional tavern) near the resort for a simple dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café near resort — pastel de nata (custard tart) + coffee for €2-3
meals.lunch: Local mercado or bakery — prego sandwich (beef roll) or bifana for €3-5
meals.dinner: Tasca dinner — grilled sardines with bread and salad, house wine included for €10-14 per person

day_by_day.notes: September is shoulder season — great weather, fewer crowds than August, and slightly lower prices. Always ask for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) at restaurants for the best budget value.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia da Marinha or Praia do Camilo (two of the Algarve's most stunning beaches with dramatic limestone cliffs). Take a local bus or rent a bicycle. Arrive early to secure a good spot and enjoy snorkeling in the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby sea caves and grottos by renting a kayak or joining a shared boat tour (budget tours start around €15-20 per person). The sea caves near Lagos are world-famous and a must-see. Alternatively, walk the clifftop trails for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl) to pick up affordable Portuguese wine (€3-6 per bottle) and local cheeses for a budget beach picnic sunset session.

meals.breakfast: Resort café or nearby pastelaria — toast with butter and jam + coffee for €2-4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the supermarket — local bread, canned tuna, olives, fruit for €4-6
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant — cataplana (seafood stew) shared between two people for €12-15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals typically run €10-15/hour. Shared boat cave tours are more economical than private ones. Wear water shoes as some beach access involves rocky paths.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Take the local bus (€2-4 each way). Visit the Ponta da Piedade viewpoint for breathtaking golden cliff formations and turquoise water. Walk the free clifftop trail along the coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town: the Slave Market Museum (€3 entry), Igreja de Santo António (€4 entry), and the town walls. Browse the local artisan shops for handmade ceramics and cork products. Relax at Meia Praia — a long, wide beach perfect for afternoon swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos nightlife on a budget — the town has a lively but affordable bar scene. Many bars offer happy hour deals from 6-8pm. Try a caipirinha or local Super Bock beer for €2-3 each.

meals.breakfast: Lagos café — galão (milky coffee) and croissant for €2-3
meals.lunch: Lagos market hall or snack bar — grilled chicken piri-piri wrap for €5-7
meals.dinner: Lagos restaurant — bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes) for €9-13

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is extremely walkable. The bus from most Algarve resort areas is frequent and cheap. The Ponta da Piedade viewpoint is free and absolutely unmissable — go in the afternoon light for best photos.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning! Visit a local Algarve winery. The Algarve wine region (DOC Algarve) produces excellent reds and whites from indigenous grapes like Negra Mole. Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar or Adega do Cantor are well-regarded. Many offer free or low-cost tastings (€5-10) with advance booking.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, explore the nearby village of Ferragudo — a picturesque whitewashed fishing village with a castle, narrow streets, and a lovely beach. It's quieter and less touristy than Albufeira. Walk to Praia Grande de Ferragudo for an afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ferragudo village — fresh fish and seafood at a local restaurant overlooking the estuary. The views of Portimão across the river are magical at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pastelaria near resort — €3-5
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery (if offered) or packed lunch from supermarket — €5-8
meals.dinner: Ferragudo seafood restaurant — grilled sea bass (robalo) with vegetables and local wine for €13-18

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to book winery visits — many require reservations. Some wineries offer free tastings if you purchase a bottle. Ferragudo is accessible by local bus or a short taxi ride from Portimão (approx €8-10).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Benagil — one of Portugal's most iconic beaches, famous for its sea cave (Algar de Benagil). Take a shared boat tour from Carvoeiro (€15-20) or rent a kayak/SUP board to paddle into the cave. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Carvoeiro village — a charming cliff-top resort town with a small beach, colorful fishing boats, and excellent viewpoints at Telheiro and Algar Seco rock formations (free to visit). Walk the boardwalk along the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort area. Cook a simple dinner using local ingredients from the supermarket — fresh Algarve tomatoes, local cheese, olives, cured meats, and a good bottle of Algarve wine for a relaxed evening on the balcony or terrace.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Carvoeiro — pastel de nata and coffee for €2-3
meals.lunch: Carvoeiro snack bar — tosta mista (grilled ham and cheese sandwich) and fresh juice for €5-7
meals.dinner: Self-catered balcony dinner — supermarket provisions (cheese, charcuterie, bread, wine) for €8-12 total

day_by_day.notes: Benagil cave is extremely popular — weekday mornings are less crowded. Swimming into the cave is not recommended due to boat traffic; take a tour or kayak. Carvoeiro is accessible by bus from most Algarve towns.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint rest and beach day at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront. Spend the morning relaxing on the beach, swimming, and reading. September sun is warm but not overwhelming — perfect beach weather. Explore the immediate coastal area on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (€10-15/day from local shops) and cycle along the coastal bike paths. Many Algarve towns have dedicated cycling routes with stunning ocean views. Explore hidden coves and viewpoints not accessible by bus.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local adega (wine cellar/bar) for an informal wine tasting session. Many small local wine bars offer tasting flights of 3-5 Algarve wines for €8-15. Ask the barkeeper for food pairing recommendations.

meals.breakfast: Resort café or nearby bakery — full Portuguese breakfast (eggs, ham, bread, coffee) for €5-7
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — fresh fruit, yogurt, and a bifana sandwich for €6-8
meals.dinner: Local adega wine bar — shared charcuterie and cheese board with wine tasting for €15-20 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to do laundry at the resort or a local laundromat (€4-6 per load) and repack for the second week. Check local event listings — September often has harvest festivals and local feiras (fairs).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take the train from the nearest station (€3-5 each way) or local bus. Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (€3 entry) with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (free entry), the Archaeological Museum (€2), and the charming town center. Browse the local market for fresh Algarve oranges, figs, and almonds — the region is famous for these. Visit a local cork factory or shop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Dine at a local tasca using ingredients you may have picked up at the Silves market. Alternatively, find a beachside restaurant for a relaxed end to the day.

meals.breakfast: Train station café or resort — coffee and pastry for €2-3
meals.lunch: Silves restaurant — prato do dia (daily special) with soup, main, and drink for €9-12
meals.dinner: Resort area tasca — frango assado (roast chicken) with fries and salad for €10-14

day_by_day.notes: Silves is inland — it can be slightly hotter than the coast. Bring water and sunscreen. The castle is one of the best-preserved Moorish fortifications in Portugal and well worth the entry fee. September is harvest season — the town may have special events.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe. Take a bus from Lagos (€4-6 return). Cabo de São Vicente has dramatic 75-meter cliffs and a historic lighthouse. It's one of the most powerful natural sights in all of Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres Fortress (€3 entry) — a historic promontory fort used by Henry the Navigator. Walk the windswept cliffs. Sagres town has a laid-back surfer vibe with affordable cafés and restaurants. Check out Praia do Martinhal for a beautiful sheltered beach.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Sagres sunset at Cabo de São Vicente — it's said to be one of the best sunsets in Europe. The lighthouse silhouette against the orange sky is unforgettable. Return to resort by evening bus.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from resort or grab from a bakery before the bus — €3-5
meals.lunch: Sagres café or snack bar — fresh tuna sandwich and local beer for €7-10
meals.dinner: Sagres or Lagos restaurant on the way back — ameijoas à bulhão pato (clams in garlic and wine) for €12-16

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. The last bus back to Lagos typically leaves around 7-8pm; check the schedule in advance. The round trip from most Algarve resorts via Lagos takes most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit the Algarve wine route (Rota dos Vinhos do Algarve). Head to the Lagoa wine region, which is the heart of Algarve wine production. Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa offers affordable tastings and cellar tours (€5-10). Sample local varieties including Crato Branco and Negra Mole.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, visit Lagoa town center and then head to Praia de Carvoeiro or Praia do Paraíso for a relaxed beach afternoon. The beaches near Lagoa are beautiful and less crowded than the main tourist spots.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a relaxing evening. Buy a bottle of your favorite wine from the day's tasting and enjoy it on the beach at sunset. Many resorts have beach bars that allow you to bring your own wine with a small corkage fee, or simply sit on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café — yogurt with honey and granola + coffee for €4-6
meals.lunch: Winery lunch or Lagoa market — local bread, cheese, and wine for €6-10
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant near resort — arroz de marisco (seafood rice) shared for two for €13-18 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Lagoa wine cooperative is one of the most budget-friendly tasting experiences in the Algarve. They often sell bottles at cellar prices significantly cheaper than retail. Stock up on a few bottles to enjoy throughout the rest of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Portimão — the Algarve's second-largest city. Take a local bus or train. Explore the revitalized waterfront and the excellent Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, €3 other days) — a fascinating museum set in a former sardine canning factory, telling the story of the local fishing industry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo for a second visit or explore Portimão's Praia da Rocha — a wide, dramatic beach backed by ochre cliffs and a 16th-century fortress. The beach is large enough to find a quiet spot even in September.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its sardine grilling culture. Head to the riverside restaurants near the old fish market for the best grilled sardines in the Algarve — a true local experience at budget prices.

meals.breakfast: Portimão café — toasted bread with tomato and olive oil + coffee for €3-4
meals.lunch: Riverside snack bar — fresh sardine sandwich or prego for €4-6
meals.dinner: Portimão riverside restaurant — grilled sardines (6 pieces) with salad, bread, and house wine for €10-14

day_by_day.notes: Portimão's sardine restaurants are legendary. The sardine festival typically happens in August, but the tradition continues year-round. Always order the house wine (vinho da casa) — it's usually good quality and very affordable (€4-7 per bottle).

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach discovered during the trip, or try one you haven't visited yet. Praia da Luz near Lagos is beautiful and has a relaxed atmosphere. Spend the morning swimming, snorkeling, or simply soaking up the last of the Algarve sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any local shops for last-minute souvenirs. Best budget souvenirs: local wine (€4-8), Algarve honey (€4-6), dried figs and almonds (€3-5), handmade cork products (€5-15), and local olive oil (€5-8). Visit the local weekly market if one is on.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on your last night. Choose a restaurant with a sea view and order something special like percebes (barnacles), gambas al ajillo (garlic prawns), or a full seafood cataplana. Toast to a wonderful Algarve adventure with a bottle of local wine.

meals.breakfast: Resort café — full Portuguese breakfast as a treat for €6-8
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — light lunch of salad and grilled fish for €9-12
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a seafood restaurant — cataplana for two with wine for €20-25 per person (slight splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Check out supermarket closing times for last-minute wine and food purchases. Pack any liquids (wine bottles) carefully in checked luggage. Confirm your departure transport to Faro Airport for the next day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take photos, collect a small shell or pebble as a free memento. Enjoy a slow breakfast and begin packing. Check out procedures at Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, either relax at the resort until checkout or head to Faro for a few hours of exploration. Faro old town (Cidade Velha) is compact and walkable — visit the cathedral (€3.50), the bone chapel, and the charming marina area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Faro Airport. Allow extra time for check-in. Enjoy a final pastel de nata and coffee at the airport café (€2-3) as a sweet farewell to Portugal.

meals.breakfast: Resort or nearby café — final Portuguese breakfast for €4-6
meals.lunch: Faro town café or airport — light meal or sandwich for €6-10
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight — budget €8-12 for airport food if needed

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport is small and manageable. Arrive at least 2 hours before departure. The EVA Bus from most Algarve towns to Faro Airport costs €2-5. Taxis cost €15-30 depending on distance. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and accommodation): €600-900 for 13 days including food, transport, activities, and wine tastings.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning coastlines along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail, stopping at Praia da Marinha's golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear turquoise waters for swimming and snorkeling among sea caves and rock arches.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffside Experience
experiences.description: Visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, and the historic Sagres Fortress at golden hour. Watch the sun dip into the Atlantic from towering 75-meter cliffs while exploring the 15th-century fortress used by Henry the Navigator.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Travel day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Travel day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 30–45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and unwind at the resort bar with a light nightcap.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or sandwich at Faro Airport arrivals hall, or order room service at the resort upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 simple – arrival is late at night. Pre-arrange airport transfer with the resort or book a reputable taxi/Uber in advance. Pack a light snack for the ride. Rest well for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings and soak in the stunning Algarve coastline. Dip your toes in the Atlantic for the first time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort beach or pool – decompress from travel, read, and enjoy the warm September sun. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella if not included. The sea in September is beautifully warm (~22°C).
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town center for your first proper Portuguese dinner. Explore the local promenade and enjoy the relaxed Algarve atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – included or à la carte at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort beach bar – grilled fish sandwich, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Casa do Polvo or a local tasca in town – try Cataplana de Marisco (seafood stew) and a glass of Alentejo white wine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery and orientation day. No rushing – the Algarve rewards those who slow down. September is shoulder season: fewer crowds, warm weather, and lower prices than peak July/August.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim – Start early (9:00 AM) to beat the heat. Drive or taxi to Praia da Marinha (~20–30 min from most Algarve beach resorts). Begin the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos), a 5.7 km clifftop trail with breathtaking sea arches, grottos, and golden limestone formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water – consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Pack snorkeling gear if possible; the underwater rock formations are spectacular. Relax on the beach and have a picnic lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Shower and head out for dinner in a nearby beach town. Enjoy a sunset drink at a cliffside bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – fuel up well before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Continente) – local cheese, presunto, crusty bread, fruit, and water (~€8–12) OR the small beach snack bar at Marinha
meals.dinner: O Lourenço or similar seafood restaurant in Lagoa/Carvoeiro – grilled sea bass (Robalo) with roasted potatoes and local vinho verde (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the coastal trail – the path has uneven limestone terrain. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 1.5L of water per person. The trail is moderately easy but exposed to sun. Parking at Praia da Marinha can fill up – arrive before 9:30 AM or take a taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Silves – the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves, ~€3 entry), walk the medieval walls, and explore the Gothic Cathedral. The town is surrounded by orange and almond groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience in the Silves/Lagoa wine region. Visit Adega do Cantor (owned by Cliff Richard) or Quinta dos Vales winery for a guided tour and tasting of regional Algarve wines including Negra Mole and Aragonez varieties. Most tastings include 4–6 wines with local charcuterie (~€15–25 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Silves old town before returning to the resort. The town has a lovely riverside atmosphere along the Arade River.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves – a charming café inside the castle walls serving light lunches and pastries (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui in Silves – a legendary local institution for grilled fish and seafood platters (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the winery tour in advance, especially for weekends. Quinta dos Vales offers excellent English-language tours. Silves is approximately 30–45 minutes inland from the coast – a great contrast to the beach days. Designated driver recommended if doing wine tasting, or arrange a taxi/tour pickup.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Benagil – one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches. Arrive early by 9:00 AM to rent a kayak or paddleboard and paddle into the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil), a stunning natural cathedral with a hole in the ceiling open to the sky. Book a guided boat tour if you prefer not to kayak (~€10–15).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coast to Praia de Albandeira or Praia do Carvalho – smaller, quieter cove beaches perfect for snorkeling and relaxing. Pack lunch and make a half-day beach hop out of it.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy the resort facilities – pool, spa if available. Have dinner at the resort restaurant for a relaxed evening in.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – pack some fruit and pastries to go
meals.lunch: Beach picnic or the Benagil beach snack bar – fresh grilled sardines, bread, and local beer (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant – try the catch of the day with Algarve-style clam rice (Arroz de Amêijoas) and a bottle of Alentejo red (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil Cave can ONLY be entered by water (swimming, kayak, or small boat) – no access by foot. Arrive very early on weekends as it gets crowded. September is still busy on Saturdays. Life jackets are provided with kayak rentals. The cave interior is magical – bring a waterproof phone case for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Lagos – one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Explore the cobblestone old town, the 16th-century city walls, the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos – the world's first slave market, sobering but important), and the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning azulejo tilework.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Meia Praia (a long, wide sandy beach north of Lagos) or take the short ferry/water taxi to the dramatic Ponta da Piedade rock formations and sea caves. Hire a small boat tour from the Lagos marina to explore the sea arches (~€15–20 per person, 45 min).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner and enjoy the lively Sunday evening atmosphere. Lagos has an excellent restaurant scene and a vibrant but relaxed bar street.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: : Tasca do Zé in Lagos old town – traditional Portuguese lunch with pork cheeks (bochechas) or grilled fish and house wine (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: No Patio or Casinha do Petisco in Lagos – tapas-style sharing plates, regional cheeses, and a bottle of local Algarve rosé (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 45–60 minutes west of central Algarve. Consider driving or taking the regional train from Faro/Albufeira if your resort is in the eastern Algarve. The Ponta da Piedade boat tours run until approximately 18:00 – time your afternoon accordingly. Sunday can be quieter for sightseeing but busier for restaurants – book dinner in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full western Algarve day: Drive to Sagres (30 min from Lagos, 1.5 hrs from central Algarve). Visit the Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres, ~€3 entry) – the historic base of Henry the Navigator's school of exploration. Walk the dramatic clifftop and feel the raw power of the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagres Sunset Cliffside Experience – Drive 6 km to Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Stand on the edge of the world at the lighthouse and feel the wind off the Atlantic. This is one of the most dramatic and moving landscapes in all of Portugal. Browse the artisan market stalls selling local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Sagres sunset from the cliffs – the sun drops directly into the Atlantic Ocean here, creating extraordinary colors. This is one of the most spectacular sunsets in Europe. Drive back to the resort afterward.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – early start recommended
meals.lunch: A Sagres – the town's namesake restaurant near the port, serving fresh local tuna (atum) which Sagres is famous for, with local bread and salad (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dromedário in Sagres or stop in Lagos on the way back – grilled octopus (polvo grelhado) and Alentejo red wine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente is extremely windy – bring a light jacket even in September. The sunset here is world-famous; plan to arrive at least 45 minutes before sunset for the best spot. Sunset in mid-September is approximately 20:00. The drive back to central Algarve after sunset will be dark – drive carefully on the EN125 road.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and resort morning – sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend the morning at the pool or beach. This is a mid-trip recovery day. Read, swim, and simply enjoy the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: Take a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson on the beach (~€30–40/hr with instructor) or rent bikes and cycle along the coastal bike path. Alternatively, book a resort spa treatment for the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar near the resort. Try a Portuguese Ginjinha (cherry liqueur) or a Medronho (local arbutus berry spirit) as an aperitif.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – take your time
meals.lunch: Resort beach bar or a nearby beachfront café – prego sandwich (steak roll) or fresh grilled sardines with salad (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: Local mid-range restaurant near resort – try Bacalhau à Brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potato crisps) – a quintessential Portuguese dish (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are important for a balanced itinerary. Don't feel obligated to fill every moment – the Algarve is best enjoyed at a relaxed pace. September weather is typically sunny with temperatures around 25–28°C – perfect beach weather.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Tavira – widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Cross the Roman bridge over the Gilão River, visit the 37 churches (start with Igreja da Misericórdia), and explore the Moorish castle ruins with panoramic views over the terracotta rooftops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Quatro Águas to Ilha de Tavira – a pristine barrier island beach in the Ria Formosa Natural Park. The beaches here are wild, unspoiled, and backed by sand dunes. Swim in the calm, shallow lagoon-side waters or the open Atlantic.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira old town – one of the best restaurant scenes in the Algarve. Stroll the riverside promenade as the evening lights reflect on the water.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Ilha de Tavira beach – grilled fish, cold drinks, and ice cream (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica or O Corvo in Tavira – clam cataplana or grilled red mullet (salmonete) with local Alentejo wine (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 30–40 minutes east of Faro. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs regularly (~€2 return) and takes 10 minutes. The island has no permanent residents – just beaches, dunes, and a few seasonal beach bars. Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-recognized wetland and birdwatching paradise. Bring binoculars if interested in wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Wine and food experience day: Drive north into the Alentejo wine region (approximately 1.5 hrs from the Algarve coast). Visit Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous near Beja – two of Portugal's most celebrated wine estates. Enjoy a guided vineyard tour and barrel tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a full sit-down wine pairing lunch at the estate restaurant (book in advance). Alentejo wines – particularly the reds made from Aragonez, Trincadeira, and Alicante Bouschet – are world-class. The landscape of rolling cork oak forests and golden plains is stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to the Algarve coast. Stop in the town of Ourique or Almodôvar for a coffee and pastry break. Return to the resort for a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – early start for the drive
meals.lunch: Estate restaurant wine pairing lunch at Herdade do Esporão – 3-course seasonal menu with 4 wine pairings (~€45–60 per person, book ahead)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort or a simple local tasca – soup, bread, and cheese after the big lunch (~€15–20)

day_by_day.notes: This is the dedicated wine day – the highlight for wine enthusiasts. Book the Esporão estate tour and lunch at least 1 week in advance (esporao.com). Designate a driver or arrange a private driver/tour for the day (~€80–120 for a private driver from the Algarve). Alentejo wine is significantly different from Algarve wine – bigger, bolder reds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Albufeira – the Algarve's most popular resort town. Visit the Old Town (Cidade Velha) area, the fishermen's beach (Praia dos Pescadores), and the vibrant morning market. Browse local ceramics, cork products, and lace at the craft stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jeep safari or off-road tour into the Algarve interior (Serra do Caldeirão hills). Several operators offer half-day 4x4 tours through whitewashed villages, cork oak forests, and citrus orchards (~€45–65 per person). See rural Algarve life that most tourists never experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a final sunset swim at the beach. Book a special dinner for tonight – a slightly elevated dining experience to celebrate the penultimate full day.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Snack during the jeep safari – most tours include a stop at a rural quinta for local bread, cheese, honey, and medronho spirit
meals.dinner: Vila Joya (if budget allows for a splurge – 2 Michelin stars, ~€150–200 per person) OR a quality local restaurant like Restaurante Veneza in Albufeira – fresh Atlantic lobster or T-bone steak with a premium Alentejo red (~€40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The jeep safari is excellent for seeing the authentic, non-touristy Algarve. Book with a reputable operator like Mega Jeep Tours or Zoomarine Jeep Safari. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting dusty. Friday evening in Albufeira is lively – the old town has excellent energy.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning – return to your favorite beach from the trip or try somewhere new. Praia da Falésia (near Albufeira) is spectacular – dramatic red and orange ochre cliffs stretching 6 km, with fine golden sand. Perfect for a long morning walk and final swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and exploration. Visit a local market or artisan shop for Portuguese tiles (azulejos), cork products, local wine bottles, fleur de sel (Algarve sea salt), almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), and local ceramics. Pack purchases carefully for the flight home.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner – choose the best restaurant from your trip for a return visit, or try something you haven't yet. Enjoy a final bottle of Portuguese wine and toast to a wonderful Algarve holiday.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach bar at Praia da Falésia – fresh seafood, cold beer, and a long relaxed lunch (~€20–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top local restaurant – splurge slightly on a seafood mixed grill (marisqueira) with a premium bottle of Alentejo or Douro red wine (~€40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy wine to take home – Portuguese wine is exceptional value. Most airports allow 1–2 bottles in checked luggage (wrap carefully). Dom Rodrigo almond sweets from Algarve are the perfect edible souvenir. Check your airline's baggage rules for liquids and fragile items. Enjoy every last moment of the Algarve sunshine.

day_by_day.morning: Final resort breakfast – take your time and savor it. Take a last walk on the beach or sit with a coffee watching the Atlantic. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout 11:00–12:00). If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, store luggage with the concierge and enjoy a final few hours. Visit Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha) near the airport – the walled medieval center, the Cathedral (Sé de Faro), and the famous Bone Chapel (Igreja dos Ossos) are all walkable and close to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Faro Airport. Allow 2 hours before departure. Browse duty-free for last-minute Portuguese wine, pastéis de nata, and Compal juices. Depart Portugal with wonderful memories.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – enjoy it fully
meals.lunch: Café Aliança or Faro Old Town café – a final pastel de nata (custard tart) and galão (Portuguese latte) (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or café at Faro Airport if flight is in the evening

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport (FAO) is compact and efficient – 90 minutes before departure is usually sufficient, but 2 hours is recommended for international flights. The Bone Chapel in Faro is a unique and memorable final stop – free entry, 10 minutes from the airport. Confirm your return flight details the night before. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning coastlines along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail, stopping at Praia da Marinha's golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear turquoise waters for swimming and snorkeling among sea caves and rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit boutique wineries in the Lagoa wine region, tasting local Algarve DOC wines including Arinto, Negra Mole, and Syrah varieties. Guided tours include cellar visits, food pairings with local cheeses and charcuterie, and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through dramatic sea caves and grottos along the Algarve coastline, culminating at the famous Benagil Cave with its natural skylight dome. A guided kayak tour offers access to hidden beaches and sea arches unreachable on foot.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffside Experience
experiences.description: Visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, and the historic Sagres Fortress at golden hour. Watch the sun dip into the Atlantic from towering 75-meter cliffs while exploring the 15th-century fortress used by Henry the Navigator.

experiences.name: Quinta do Francês Organic Wine Tasting
experiences.description: Experience an intimate organic winery tasting session at one of the Algarve's most acclaimed small-production estates. Sample award-winning red and white wines paired with local Algarve honey, figs, and artisan bread while learning about sustainable viticulture practices.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Travel Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, welcome drink at the resort bar, and light late-night snack service. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack board at the resort's private lounge – charcuterie, local cheeses, Algarve olives, and a glass of sparkling Alvarinho upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. No activities scheduled given the 22:30 arrival. Request early turndown service and a late breakfast slot for the following morning to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort followed by a private orientation walk along the beachfront. Spend the late morning on the resort's exclusive beach, acclimatizing to the stunning Algarve coastline. Enjoy the warm September sea and resort amenities including infinity pool and cabana service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby coastal town of Carvoeiro on foot – browse the boutiques, visit the Carvoeiro beach viewpoint, and enjoy the charming whitewashed cliffside architecture. Arrange a private boat charter from Carvoeiro Marina for a 2-hour coastal cruise along the golden limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the resort terrace overlooking the Atlantic. Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring modern Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant – pastéis de nata, fresh tropical fruits, smoked fish, artisan breads, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside chiringuito in Carvoeiro – grilled sea bass, local salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant – tasting menu featuring Algarve cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), octopus carpaccio, and paired with regional DOC wines

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) with minimal rain – ideal beach conditions. Book the private boat charter the evening before through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour – Depart mid-morning with a private guide to the Lagoa wine region. Visit two boutique wineries, learning about the unique terroir of the Algarve DOC. Taste local varietals including Arinto, Negra Mole, and Syrah blends directly from the barrel and bottle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with a vineyard picnic lunch among the vines. Visit a second acclaimed winery for a reserve tasting and cellar tour. Purchase select bottles to enjoy throughout the trip. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort spa – indulge in a 60-minute deep tissue or hot stone massage. Freshen up and enjoy a private in-suite dinner arranged by the resort chef, paired with wines acquired during the day's tour.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort – eggs Benedict with smoked Algarve tuna, freshly baked croissants, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Vineyard picnic curated by the winery – artisan charcuterie, regional cheeses, fresh bread, and paired wine flights al fresco among the vines
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience – chef-curated 4-course Portuguese tasting menu with your personally selected vineyard wines

day_by_day.notes: The Lagoa wine region is approximately 15–20 minutes from most Carvoeiro/Lagoa area resorts. Pre-book the wine tour through the resort concierge or directly with the winery for a fully private, guided experience.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim – Depart early morning with a certified private guide for the legendary Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos). Trek the dramatic clifftop path above turquoise waters, stopping at multiple viewpoints for photography and exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the secluded Praia da Marinha – consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Swim in the crystal-clear rock pool coves, snorkel among the limestone arches, and relax on the golden sands with a private beach picnic. Return to the resort by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort beach bar. Dinner at a premium local restaurant in Lagoa or Carvoeiro specializing in traditional Algarvian cuisine with a contemporary twist.

meals.breakfast: Early energizing breakfast at the resort – granola, Greek yogurt, smoked salmon on sourdough, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Luxury beach picnic prepared by the resort – lobster rolls, chilled gazpacho, fresh fruit skewers, sparkling water, and a bottle of chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Terraço or equivalent premium local restaurant – grilled whole Dourada (sea bream), Algarve-style amêijoas (clams), and local dessert medley with a bottle of regional white wine

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is approximately 5.7 km and takes 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen. The trail begins near Praia de Vale Centianes – a short drive from the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour – Join a private guided kayak tour departing from Benagil Beach. Paddle through dramatic sea caves, grottos, and natural arches along one of the Algarve's most spectacular coastlines. Enter the famous Benagil Cave (Algar de Benagil) – a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight opening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-kayak relaxation on Praia de Benagil. Arrange a private speedboat transfer back along the coast to Carvoeiro. Afternoon at leisure at the resort – pool, spa, or simply enjoying the beachfront. Optional: book a 90-minute resort spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Dress elegantly for dinner at one of the Algarve's most celebrated fine-dining establishments. Reserve a table at a Michelin-starred or equivalent restaurant in the region.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet breakfast – fuel up before the morning kayak adventure with eggs, fresh pastries, smoked fish, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at Benagil – fresh grilled sardines, local bread, and chilled Alvarinho wine at a traditional tasca
meals.dinner: Fine-dining experience at Bon Bon Restaurant (Carvoeiro, Michelin-starred) or equivalent – innovative Portuguese tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the private kayak tour at least 48 hours in advance. September conditions are generally ideal for sea kayaking with calm Atlantic swells. The Benagil Cave can only be accessed by sea – no land access exists. Michelin restaurant reservations should be made weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort. Indulge in a late breakfast followed by a private yoga or Pilates session on the beach terrace arranged through the resort's wellness program. Spend time reading, swimming, and enjoying the resort's full luxury amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to the historic town of Silves – the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) and the Gothic Cathedral. Explore the charming cobblestone streets, artisan shops, and local markets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset. Enjoy a private wine tasting session on your suite's terrace – arranged by the concierge with a curated selection of Algarve DOC and Alentejo wines accompanied by local tapas.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte brunch at the resort – avocado toast with Algarve prawns, eggs any style, fresh pastries, and mimosas
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch in Silves at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui or equivalent – grilled mixed seafood platter, regional salads, and local wine
meals.dinner: In-suite private terrace dining – resort chef prepares a personalized 3-course dinner with curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 20–25 minutes from Carvoeiro/Lagoa area. The castle entrance fee is minimal. September is post-peak tourist season, making it an ideal time to explore without crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Quinta do Francês Organic Wine Tasting – Private morning transfer to Quinta do Francês, one of the Algarve's most acclaimed small-production organic wineries. Enjoy an intimate guided tour of the organic vineyard, learning about sustainable viticulture practices and the unique microclimate of the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Extended tasting session at Quinta do Francês – sample reserve wines, barrel samples, and limited-edition releases. Enjoy a farm-to-table lunch on the estate. Browse and purchase wines to take home. Return to the resort mid-afternoon. Spend the remainder of the afternoon at the beach or pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the resort's private beach. Dinner at a premium seafood restaurant in Portimão or Ferragudo – known for their exceptional fresh catch and traditional cataplana cooking.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – light continental spread with local honey, artisan jams, fresh fruit, and espresso before departing for the winery
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table estate lunch at Quinta do Francês – organic vegetable dishes, local cheeses, charcuterie, and paired organic wines in a vineyard setting
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo or equivalent – fresh Atlantic catch, traditional cataplana de peixe, and local wines with a river estuary view

day_by_day.notes: Quinta do Francês is a small-production winery – private tastings must be booked well in advance. The estate produces limited quantities and is known for exceptional quality. Ferragudo is a picturesque fishing village approximately 15 minutes from Carvoeiro.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise beach walk and wild swimming session along the resort's beachfront – the September light is golden and the water temperature is at its annual warmest. Follow with a resort spa morning: hammam ritual, exfoliation treatment, and relaxation pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the western Algarve coast – private driver to Praia da Rocha in Portimão for a leisurely stroll along the wide golden beach and impressive cliff formations. Visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão) – an award-winning museum housed in a former sardine canning factory.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a premium cocktail experience at the bar. Enjoy a chef's table dinner at the resort – an exclusive behind-the-scenes culinary experience where the head chef prepares a personalized menu at a private table in or adjacent to the kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Post-spa breakfast at the resort wellness café – acai bowls, smoked salmon bagels, fresh juices, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Portimão overlooking the river – grilled tiger prawns, fresh bread, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at the resort – exclusive 6-course tasting menu with wine pairing, prepared and presented personally by the executive chef

day_by_day.notes: The chef's table experience should be booked with the resort at least 3–4 days in advance as it is a limited-availability exclusive. The Portimão Museum is excellent and free on the first Sunday of each month.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente – depart after breakfast with a private driver for the dramatic southwestern tip of Europe. Visit the historic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress steeped in Age of Discovery history. Walk the windswept ramparts with panoramic Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagres Sunset Cliffside Experience – Continue to Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Stand at the dramatic 75-meter-high cliffs where the Atlantic stretches endlessly to the horizon. Visit the lighthouse and explore the headland. Enjoy the wild, rugged beauty of this iconic location.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the spectacular sunset from the cliffs of Cabo de São Vicente – one of the most dramatic sunsets in all of Europe. Dinner in Sagres village at a premium restaurant before the private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before the long day trip – eggs, pastries, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sagres at A Sagres or Restaurante Vila Velha – fresh grilled fish, local clams, and regional wine
meals.dinner: Premium dinner in Sagres at Restaurante Vila Velha or equivalent – grilled lobster, fresh catch of the day, and a bottle of Alentejo red wine before the return drive

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1.5 hours from Carvoeiro/Lagoa area – a full day trip is recommended. September evenings can be breezy at Cabo de São Vicente – bring a light jacket. The sunset here is legendary and not to be missed. Private driver allows flexibility with timing.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and resort immersion day. Begin with a 7 AM beach meditation session followed by a resort spa half-day package – choose from hot stone massage, aromatherapy facial, and hydrotherapy circuit. Completely unplug and recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sailing charter from Carvoeiro or Portimão Marina – a 4-hour luxury catamaran or sailboat experience along the Algarve coastline. Sail past sea caves, hidden beaches, and golden cliffs. Swim and snorkel in secluded coves accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort sun-kissed and refreshed. Sunset cocktails at the resort infinity pool bar. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the nearby village of Lagoa – exploring the local dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-spa breakfast at the resort wellness café – smoothie bowls, fresh fruit, herbal tea, and light pastries
meals.lunch: Onboard catered lunch on the sailing charter – fresh seafood, salads, chilled rosé, and tropical fruits served on deck
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Avenida in Lagoa or equivalent – traditional Algarvian cuisine, local wines, and a warm village atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Private sailing charters can be arranged through the resort concierge or directly with Carvoeiro/Portimão Marina operators. September sea conditions are typically excellent for sailing. Request a sunset return time to maximize the golden hour on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the eastern Algarve – private driver to the stunning Ria Formosa Natural Park near Faro. Take a private guided boat tour through the lagoon system, visiting barrier islands, salt pans rich with birdlife, and pristine sandbar beaches only accessible by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the beautiful island beach of Ilha Deserta (Barreta Island) – the most remote and pristine barrier island in the Ria Formosa. Spend the afternoon on this stunning, almost deserted beach with crystal-clear lagoon waters. Return by boat to Faro and explore the charming old town briefly.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via private transfer. Final evening at leisure – optional: arrange a private beach bonfire experience through the resort with champagne, local cheeses, and live acoustic guitar music.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – eggs Benedict, smoked fish platter, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at the exclusive Estaminé Restaurant on Ilha Deserta – one of the most unique dining locations in Portugal, serving fresh seafood on a deserted island
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner at the resort – grilled seafood, local breads, artisan cheeses, and premium Algarve wines under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Ria Formosa is approximately 45–50 minutes from the Lagoa/Carvoeiro area. The Estaminé Restaurant on Ilha Deserta is exceptional and requires advance reservations – book through the resort concierge. The private beach bonfire must be arranged with resort management in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day – spend the entire morning on the resort's private beachfront. Arrange premium cabana service with chilled towels, fresh fruit, and drinks. Take one final swim in the warm Atlantic waters. Optional: sunrise paddleboard or stand-up paddleboard session arranged through the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon combining last-minute souvenir shopping in Carvoeiro village – artisan ceramics, local wines, Algarve sea salt, and traditional pottery. Return to the resort for a final spa treatment or relaxation by the pool. Begin light packing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's finest restaurant – request a premium table with ocean view. Celebrate the journey with a special tasting menu and a bottle of vintage Algarve or Douro wine. Reminisce over the highlights of 13 days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Champagne brunch at the resort – celebrate the final full day with a lavish spread including smoked salmon, oysters, pastries, fresh fruit, and sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar – grilled prawns, fresh salads, and a final glass of chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant – premium 7-course tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairing, finishing with a dessert wine and petit fours

day_by_day.notes: Reserve the farewell dinner table with the best ocean view well in advance – request it at check-in. Consider purchasing a case of Algarve DOC wines from the resort's wine cellar to ship home as a lasting memory of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Take a slow, mindful walk along the beach one final time. Complete packing and check-out formalities. Resort concierge arranges private luxury transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Arrive with ample time for check-in and enjoy the airport lounge before the return flight.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – a leisurely and indulgent last meal featuring all your favorite items from the past 13 days: pastéis de nata, smoked fish, fresh fruit, and a final perfectly pulled Portuguese espresso
meals.lunch: Light snack at the Faro Airport lounge or a quick bite at a café near the airport if time allows
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer timing with the resort concierge the evening before. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for Faro Airport check-in and security. Request a late check-out (12:00–13:00) from the resort if your flight timing permits. Ensure all purchased wines are properly packed or shipped.
